items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn’t feel like I had caused my band director’s death.

ctx.x: We’re jumping ahead here. But many years later, as he’s seen that you’ve been extremely successful, was he able to kind of swallow his pride there and acknowledge that...

Well, he died some years later, I think from a heart attack probably, and, I’ll be honest, for a long time I felt like I had caused his heart attack. I’m serious. There was something inside me. I felt like I had just bothered him, bugged him, irritated him, even though I was out of school for a long time afterward. I mentioned that in my Sunday School class one time, and a lady who was in the band, she sat next to me playing saxophone, she said, “Oh, Jamey, Mr. Myers had all kinds of physical problems; you didn’t…
That’s a heck of a burden to carry with you.
